records.text: The board gave the proposal short shrift, and the CFO was left to carry the can.

artifact.comprehensible: The board dealt with the proposal quickly and without much attention, and the CFO was left to take the blame.

glosses.gloss: dealt with the proposal quickly and without giving it much attention or consideration
glosses.example: The manager gave my idea short shrift and moved on to the next topic.

glosses.gloss: take the blame or responsibility for something that went wrong
glosses.example: After the project failed, the team leader had to carry the can.

artifact.translation: 董事会草草处理了该提案，首席财务官只好背黑锅。

records.text: He bottled it at the last minute and threw his colleagues under the bus.

artifact.comprehensible: At the last minute, he lost his nerve and did something that harmed his colleagues, even though they trusted him.

glosses.gloss: lost your courage and failed to do something you were supposed to do
glosses.example: He was going to ask for a raise, but he bottled it and said nothing.

glosses.expression: threw his colleagues under the bus
glosses.gloss: did something that hurt your friends or coworkers to protect yourself
glosses.example: When the boss asked who made the mistake, she threw her team under the bus and said it was their fault.

artifact.translation: 他在最后一刻临阵退缩，还出卖了同事。

records.text: Not until the auditors had gone did the manager admit that the figures had been doctored.

artifact.comprehensible: The manager did not admit that the numbers had been changed in a dishonest way until after the auditors had left.

glosses.gloss: changed in a dishonest way to trick people
glosses.example: He doctored the photo to make it look like he was on holiday, but his friends knew he had stayed home.

glosses.gloss: people whose job is to check financial records
glosses.example: The auditors looked at all the company's accounts to make sure everything was correct.

artifact.grammar: The sentence begins with 'Not until...', which makes the main clause use inverted word order: 'did the manager admit' instead of 'the manager admitted'. This structure emphasizes that the admission happened only after the auditors left.
artifact.translation: 直到审计员离开后，经理才承认数据被篡改了。

records.text: The house stood in a state of genteel decay, its occupants having long since repaired to the Continent.

artifact.comprehensible: The house was in a state of polite, slightly shabby decay. Its residents had moved to the Continent a long time ago.

glosses.gloss: a kind of decay that is polite or upper-class, not rough or dirty
glosses.example: The old hotel showed genteel decay: the paint was faded, but the furniture was still elegant.

glosses.gloss: went to; moved to (a formal way to say 'went')
glosses.example: After the party, the guests repaired to the garden for coffee.

glosses.gloss: mainland Europe (often used by British people)
glosses.example: They sold their house in London and moved to the Continent.

artifact.grammar: The phrase 'its occupants having long since repaired to the Continent' is a participle clause. It gives a reason or background for the main clause. It means 'because its occupants had moved to the Continent a long time before'. The word 'having' shows the action was completed before the main situation.
artifact.translation: 这栋房子处于一种优雅而破败的状态，因为它的住户早已移居到欧洲大陆去了。

records.text: The findings are suggestive rather than conclusive, and ought not to be over-read.

artifact.comprehensible: The results hint at something but do not prove it, and people should not read too much into them.

glosses.gloss: hinting at something but not proving it
glosses.example: Her smile was suggestive rather than conclusive; it might have meant she was happy, or it might have meant nothing.

glosses.gloss: to understand or interpret something as having more meaning or importance than it really has
glosses.example: Don't over-read his short email; he was just busy, not angry.

artifact.translation: 这些发现只是提示性的，而非结论性的，不应当被过度解读。

records.text: The lessee shall indemnify the lessor against all claims arising from any breach of the covenants herein.

artifact.comprehensible: The person who rents the property must protect the owner from any claims that come from breaking any of the promises in this agreement.

glosses.gloss: to protect someone from loss or damage by paying for it
glosses.example: The company will indemnify you if your phone is stolen while you are at work.

glosses.gloss: the person who rents something
glosses.example: The lessee must pay the rent on the first day of each month.

glosses.gloss: the person who owns something and rents it to someone else
glosses.example: The lessor will fix the broken heater.

glosses.gloss: formal promises in a legal agreement
glosses.example: The contract has several covenants, such as keeping the garden tidy.

glosses.gloss: an act of breaking a law or agreement
glosses.example: Not paying the rent is a breach of the contract.

glosses.gloss: requests for money or demands for your rights
glosses.example: The insurance company received many claims after the storm.

glosses.gloss: coming from or caused by
glosses.example: The argument arising from the mistake made everyone upset.

artifact.grammar: The sentence uses legal language and passive-like structure. 'The lessee shall indemnify the lessor against all claims' means the lessee must protect the lessor from all claims. 'Arising from any breach of the covenants herein' tells you what kind of claims: those that come from breaking any of the promises in this document. The word 'herein' means 'in this document'.
artifact.translation: 承租人应赔偿出租人因违反本协议中的任何约定而引起的所有索赔。

records.text: The report stops short of apportioning blame, but the implications are hard to miss.

artifact.comprehensible: The report does not go as far as saying who is to blame, but it is very easy to see what it suggests.

glosses.gloss: does not go as far as; does not do something completely
glosses.example: She stopped short of calling him a liar, but everyone understood what she meant.

glosses.gloss: saying who is responsible for something bad
glosses.example: The teacher did not apportion blame for the broken window; she just asked what happened.

glosses.gloss: very easy to notice or understand
glosses.example: The sign was huge, so it was hard to miss.

artifact.translation: 报告没有直接归咎于任何人，但其暗示显而易见。

records.text: He was, to put it mildly, not best pleased with the outcome.

artifact.comprehensible: He was very unhappy with the result, to say the least.

glosses.gloss: used to say that you are describing something in a gentle way, when the truth is much stronger
glosses.example: The food was bad, to put it mildly; I couldn't eat it.

glosses.gloss: very annoyed or unhappy
glosses.example: She was not best pleased when I forgot her birthday.

artifact.translation: 说得客气一点，他对这个结果很不高兴。

records.text: What the committee had taken for a routine oversight was in fact a deliberate omission, designed to spare the minister an awkward question.

artifact.comprehensible: The committee thought it was just a normal mistake, but it was actually done on purpose. It was meant to save the minister from having to answer a difficult question.

glosses.gloss: thought to be; believed to be
glosses.example: She took the stranger for a thief, but he was just a lost tourist.

glosses.gloss: a usual mistake that happens because someone forgot to do something
glosses.example: The missing signature was a routine oversight, not a serious problem.

glosses.gloss: something left out on purpose
glosses.example: Leaving his name off the list was a deliberate omission; she did it to hurt him.

glosses.gloss: save someone from something unpleasant
glosses.example: He told a small lie to spare her feelings.

glosses.gloss: a difficult or embarrassing question
glosses.example: The reporter asked an awkward question about the money.

artifact.grammar: The sentence has a contrast: 'What the committee had taken for a routine oversight' is the subject, and 'was in fact a deliberate omission' is the main verb. The phrase 'designed to spare...' describes the omission. The structure is not too hard, but the contrast between 'routine oversight' and 'deliberate omission' is important.
artifact.translation: 委员会原以为那只是一次普通的疏忽，但实际上那是故意省略的，目的是让部长免于回答一个尴尬的问题。

records.text: The company was on the hook for a sum it could ill afford.

artifact.comprehensible: The company was responsible for paying an amount of money that it could not easily pay.

glosses.gloss: responsible for paying or dealing with something
glosses.example: After the car accident, she was on the hook for the repair costs.

glosses.expression: a sum it could ill afford
glosses.gloss: an amount of money that it could not easily pay
glosses.example: They bought a house that they could ill afford, and soon they had money problems.

artifact.translation: 公司不得不承担一笔它难以负担的款项。

records.text: The reaction proceeds only in the presence of a catalyst, without which the activation energy is prohibitively high.

artifact.comprehensible: The reaction happens only when a catalyst is there. If there is no catalyst, the activation energy is so high that the reaction cannot happen.

glosses.gloss: happens or goes forward
glosses.example: The meeting proceeds even if the manager is late.

glosses.gloss: when something is there
glosses.example: Plants grow well in the presence of sunlight.

glosses.gloss: a substance that makes a chemical reaction go faster without being used up itself
glosses.example: A catalyst helps the reaction start, but it is not part of the final product.

glosses.gloss: if it is not there
glosses.example: You need a key, without which you cannot open the door.

glosses.gloss: the energy needed to start a chemical reaction
glosses.example: The activation energy for this reaction is low, so it starts easily.

glosses.gloss: so high that it stops something from happening
glosses.example: The cost of the car was prohibitively high, so we did not buy it.

artifact.grammar: The phrase 'without which' introduces a condition: it means 'if there is no catalyst'. The main clause says the reaction happens only with a catalyst; the 'without which' clause explains what happens without it. The word 'prohibitively' modifies 'high' and means 'so high that it prevents the reaction'.
artifact.translation: 该反应只有在催化剂存在时才能进行；如果没有催化剂，活化能会高得使反应无法发生。

records.text: It behoves us to consider whether such a course of action is consonant with our obligations.

artifact.comprehensible: It is right for us to think about whether this way of doing things agrees with what we must do.

glosses.gloss: is right or proper for (someone) to do
glosses.example: It behoves you to say thank you when someone helps you.

glosses.gloss: a plan or way of doing something
glosses.example: The teacher chose a different course of action to help the students learn.

glosses.gloss: in agreement with; matching
glosses.example: His actions are consonant with his words, so I trust him.

artifact.grammar: The sentence uses 'It behoves us to consider...' where 'It' is a placeholder subject and the real subject is 'us'. This is a formal way to say 'We should consider...'. Also, 'whether such a course of action is consonant with our obligations' is a long noun clause that acts as the object of 'consider'.
artifact.translation: 我们应当考虑这样的做法是否符合我们的义务。
